name: Jamaica
snapshot: Jamaica spent 2026 rebuilding its western parishes after Hurricane Melissa, among the strongest Atlantic storms on record to make landfall.
culture: Jamaica gave the world ska, rocksteady, reggae and dancehall, and Bob Marley remains one of the most recognised people on Earth. Rastafari, born in 1930s Jamaica, spread globally through music. Its sprinters, from Usain Bolt to Shelly-Ann Fraser-Pryce, dominate world athletics. Patois is spoken by nearly everyone, alongside English.
society: Tourism, remittances and bauxite drive the economy. Jamaica has cut its debt dramatically over the past decade. Violent crime, much of it linked to gangs and politics in Kingston's garrison communities, has long been among the world's highest, though murders fell sharply in 2024 and 2025.
situation: On 28 October 2025, Hurricane Melissa came ashore in Westmoreland as a Category 5 storm, crossed western Jamaica and left over Trelawny. It was, in the prime minister's words, the third most powerful hurricane ever recorded anywhere and the most destructive ever to hit the island (Office of the Prime Minister). Jamaica spent 2026 rebuilding the west, a year after Hurricane Beryl had already battered it.

The damage was intimate and specific. Black River, a historic market town in St Elizabeth, was among the hardest hit (Jamaica Observer). Schools, police stations and clinics in the western parishes were wrecked, and the Westmoreland to St Elizabeth corridor will be rebuilt on a new alignment. Tourism, the country's lifeline, lost hotels for months; Sandals kept staff at shuttered resorts on the payroll. By March, Prime Minister Andrew Holness declared the country had moved from relief to reconstruction, with power and water largely restored, farms recovering and inflation low enough for the central bank to cut rates (JIS). The government says it has committed more than J$67 billion. The frustration that remained was slow money: in June, Holness publicly called on private insurers to pay claims faster because delays were stalling families' rebuilding (Gleaner). Planners estimated the economy might not return to its pre-Melissa output until late 2028. The deeper lesson Jamaica is absorbing is that two monster storms in two years may be the new normal for the Caribbean.
power: A parliamentary democracy and Commonwealth realm, with the British monarch represented by a governor-general. The prime minister leads the majority in the 63-seat elected House of Representatives; two parties, Holness's JLP and the PNP, alternate in power.
holders: Prime Minister Andrew Holness (JLP), re-elected for a third term in September 2025.
